- When sentiment is positive (≥0.25) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak for 3–7 days.
- If sentiment is consistently neutral or negative (≤0.00), model underestimates; add 2–5% to forecast for 7–14 days.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >10% above 18d history mean, adjust down by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30d horizon, model often lags 1–3 days behind true trend; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment is rising.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model tends to underestimate; apply 3–5% upward bias for 10–15 days.
- When sentiment spikes to 1.00, model often overreacts; reduce forecast by 5–10% for 5–7 days after spike.
